veranderings.blok: Die Aarde draai om sy as
veranderings.rede: 'heet' is formal and slightly old-fashioned for Grade 6; 'word ... genoem' is the everyday way to name a term.

veranderings.voor: Vannag in jou bed draai die Aarde om sy as
veranderings.na: Vannag, terwyl jy in jou bed lê, draai die Aarde om sy as
veranderings.rede: As written, 'in jou bed' attaches to the Earth; a short clause makes clear it is the learner who is in bed.

veranderings.blok: Wys rotasie met 'n lamp en 'n bal
veranderings.voor: die kant wat wegkyk is donker
veranderings.na: die kant wat wegkyk, is donker
veranderings.rede: AWS: a comma separates two verbs from different clauses that meet ('wegkyk, is'), which eases reading.

veranderings.blok: Wys rotasie met 'n lamp en 'n bal
veranderings.voor: 'n kol wat jy op die bal teken om die beurt
veranderings.na: 'n kol wat jy op die bal teken, om die beurt
veranderings.rede: A comma closing the relative clause shows where the subject ends and what happens to the spot begins.
The countable noun 'dag' needs the indefinite article here; without it the phrase reads clipped.

veranderings.voor: Die Aarde draai om daardie lyn. Niemand kan dit sien
veranderings.na: Die Aarde draai om daardie lyn. Niemand kan die lyn sien
veranderings.rede: Read alone, 'dit' follows a sentence whose subject is the Earth and can be taken to mean the Earth, which can be seen; naming the line removes the doubt.
